text:
neha: Heads up — since the kernel patch rolled to eu-west-2 yesterday the DCGM exporter is firing a bunch of ECC/Xid alerts. Looks like single-card blips, but they're noisy and triggering auto-drains.

alex: Saw that. Node pool euw2-gpu-batch-3 mainly. Alerts are ECC_RAW_ERRORS rising by 1 -> alert fires, then clears. Not sustained.

jamal: Is this the exporter sample-rate change from last week? We switched from 10s -> 2s in the daemonset. More sampling = more short spikes.

neha: yeah — more samples == more chance to see transient ECC counters bump. Current prometheus rule uses `increase(dcgm_ecc_raw_errors_total[1m]) > 0` which is too sensitive now.

lee: We should avoid draining unless it's a streak. Proposal: only escalate (and drain) if we see >=3 distinct ECC/Xid increments on the same GPU within 30m. Otherwise annotate and monitor.

alex: Agreed. Also need to distinguish MIG partitions vs whole-card errors — MIG infra nodes are noisy at low-level counters. For MIG nodes maybe require 5 increments to drain.

neha: Draft rule I tested locally (POC):

```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_XID_Streak
  expr: |
    sum by (instance, gpu_index) (increase(dcgm_ecc_raw_errors_total[30m])) >= 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU {{ $labels.instance }}: ECC/Xid streak on gpu {{ $labels.gpu_index }}"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-ecc-streak"
```

jamal: Nice. Using `sum by (instance, gpu_index)` makes it per-card. The `for: 5m` prevents flapping.

alex: A couple thoughts:
- We should also add `unless on()` style rule to suppress if node recently had a kernel update label `node_label: kernel_bump=true` (we don't want false positives during known churn).
- Add an annotation with last_seen_timestamp and link to node metadata.

neha: Good call. Also I'm adding a small exponential backoff for alerts in pager rules so oncall doesn't get paged on first warn. Keep page for severity=critical only.

oncall: If we reduce paging, add a slack notification to #eng-oncall and include quick triage checklist: `check dmesg, check dcgm logs, run nv-hostengine status`.

lee: Operational plan: roll rule change to staging prometheus, run `promtool test rules` and then a 24h shadow in prod (alert routed to a non-pager slack channel). If results look good, flip to primary route.

neha: Test commands I used: 
- `promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/rules/gpu_rules.yml`
- `promtool test rules /etc/prometheus/test/gpu_ecc_streak_test.yml`
- `curl -sS http://prometheus-euw2:9090/api/v1/query?query='sum%20by(instance,gpu_index)(increase(dcgm_ecc_raw_errors_total%5B30m%5D))'`

jamal: We'll also add an exporter-side flag to emit `dcgm_ecc_raw_errors_total{sampled=\"true\"}` when we observe a counter from direct sample vs derived, could help heuristics later.

alex: One more: add a daily job to scan nodes and mark ones with >30% of GPUs having repeated streaks for replacement scheduling. Put output into `infra/gpu-health` S3 path.

neha: I'll push the staging rule by EOD. Rollout plan:
1) staging rule + shadowing to #eng-infra-shadow (24h)
2) monitor tokenized metrics (alerts suppressed vs noisy)
3) tweak thresholds per MIG/non-MIG
4) enable for prod and update oncall paging

lee: 👍 Also add specific grafana panels for `increase(dcgm_ecc_raw_errors_total[30m])` per gpu_index so SREs can eyeball streaks.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: `prometheus-rule-update/gpu-ecc-streak` triggered by neha. Job ID 98712.

neha: Thanks — will post results in this thread after shadow run. If anyone has objections to the `>=3 in 30m` baseline speak now.

alex: no objections from me.

jamal: fine by infra.

lee: ok. If we still see accidental drains after this we'll raise the bar to `>=5` for MIG nodes.

neha: Closing loop: added a note to the runbook to prefer `soft-evict` over immediate `node-drain` and to set node tag `gpu:underwatch` so schedulers don't place new pods.

oncall: Copy — I'll add the triage checklist to the pager details.

neha: (later) Shadow run summary: 23 noisy single-sample alerts suppressed, 2 true streaks flagged, both traced to hardware flakiness on node euw2-gpu-batch-3-07. Created maintenance ticket INFRA-2217 for replacement.

alex: Nice outcome. Thanks everyone.
